question.prompt: Approve this implementation contract: scope is only `--setup-show` rendering of raw fixture parameters when no custom fixture IDs are present; render every such raw parameter with size-limited, exception-resilient repr-style semantics, so bytes display as `b'Hello World'` without a `BytesWarning` under `python -bb`, raw strings may observably change from `foo` to `'foo'`, and broken user `repr` implementations must not make setup-show fail; apply the same rendered behavior to setup and teardown output; preserve existing rendering of explicit and callable custom-ID results unchanged, including their current residual risk if they return bytes or otherwise unsafe values; exclude parameter-ID generation, test node IDs, `--setup-only`, and other display paths; acceptance requires a focused regression proving a bytes-parametrized test completes successfully with `--setup-show` under bytes-warning-as-error behavior and shows the repr-style bytes value during both setup and teardown, plus focused coverage proving safe bounded output for an overlong raw representation and nonfailure for a raw object whose `repr` raises, while existing custom-ID setup-show tests remain passing; implementation may choose the repository’s existing safe-representation facility or an equivalent existing facility, but may not add dependencies or broaden the affected paths. Is this complete contract approved for implementation?

acceptance_checks: A focused bytes-parametrized regression completes successfully with `--setup-show` while bytes warnings are treated as errors and displays `b'Hello World'` during both setup and teardown.
Focused coverage demonstrates bounded output for a raw parameter with an overlong representation.
Focused coverage demonstrates that a raw parameter whose `repr` raises does not make setup-show fail.
Existing setup-show tests for explicit and callable custom IDs continue to pass unchanged.

confirmed_decisions: Safe representation applies only to raw parameters stored when no custom fixture IDs exist; explicit and callable custom-ID results retain current rendering.
All raw parameters use safe repr-style semantics; the observable output for raw strings may change from unquoted to quoted text.
Raw rendering must be size-limited and resilient to exceptions raised by user-defined `repr` implementations.
Setup and teardown must display the same safely rendered raw parameter behavior.
The residual risk from unsafe explicit or callable custom-ID results is accepted and remains outside scope.
Parameter-ID generation, node IDs, `--setup-only`, and unrelated display paths are excluded.
No new dependencies may be added, and implementation must remain within the localized setup-show path.
contract.summary: Change only `--setup-show` rendering of raw fixture parameters when no custom fixture IDs are present. Render every such raw parameter with size-limited, exception-resilient repr-style semantics. Bytes must display as `b'Hello World'` without raising `BytesWarning` under `python -bb`; raw strings may consequently change from `foo` to `'foo'`; and a user object whose `repr` raises must not cause setup-show to fail. Apply the same rendering to setup and teardown. Preserve existing rendering for explicit and callable custom-ID results, including the accepted residual risk that unsafe custom-ID values such as bytes may still fail. Exclude parameter-ID generation, test node IDs, `--setup-only`, and all other display paths. Implementation may use the repository’s existing safe-representation facility or an equivalent existing facility, but must add no dependency and must not broaden the affected paths.
